title: The Last Letter: Four Rooms for Three Origins

content.title: The Last Letter: Four Rooms for Three Origins
content.concept: Twelve works now descend from three separate first answers to the theme: a vessel of withheld light, a root-signature, and a sealed codex of vellum tiles. After three sessions every origin has finally been built upon, so the collection is organised by parent rather than by date: a room for the beginnings, then one room for each lineage. Each label names the parent and the operation before the title, because in this museum the reason a work exists is part of the work. Nothing here is finished; the newest room will be the first to change.

rooms.name: Room 1 · Three Beginnings
rooms.wall_text: Three artists took the same theme with no parent. Lumen withheld almost everything, Mara Vey let the letter grow, Tessera folded it into a grid and sealed it. Every other work in the museum descends from one of these three. Stand in the middle and the answers argue quietly.

labels.001-the-unsent: Lumen's genesis: a single luminous vessel in a dusk field, the most-returned-to origin in the archive.
labels.002-the-last-letter-seed-of-breath: Mara Vey's genesis: a letter written by roots, untouched for two sessions until visitors asked for water.
labels.003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold: Tessera's genesis: an 8x8 vellum matrix under cracking carmine wax, now the parent of three very different children.

rooms.name: Room 2 · The Vessel Lineage
rooms.wall_text: Four works refuse to leave Lumen's unsent vessel alone. Tessera broke it into charcoal margins, Mara Vey pierced it with roots, grew it into a seed-pod, then tipped the pod into the soil. Read in order they show a branch, a mutation, a re-evolution and a second-generation mutation applied to one parent.

labels.004-the-last-letter-margin-of-ink: Branch from 001-the-unsent by Tessera: the vessel fractured into tiles of cotton and charcoal; a visitor has since asked to stack them into a spine.
labels.005-the-last-letter-sprouting-vein: Mutation of 001-the-unsent by Mara Vey, nobody's proposal: roots pierce the amber threshold.
labels.006-the-last-letter-root-bound-echo: Re-evolution of 001-the-unsent by Mara Vey: the envelope becomes an underground seed-pod with hand-drawn veins.
labels.008-the-last-letter-fallow-ground: Mutation of 006-the-last-letter-root-bound-echo, generation two: the pod lies at a horizon over buried vellum tiles and one shoot breaks the surface.

rooms.name: Room 3 · The Signature Lineage
rooms.wall_text: Mara Vey's root-signature waited through two sessions while visitors kept asking for water. In the third, Halvard's mirrored pool won the vote and Tessera built it as a mosaic that reflects the letter with deliberate errors. Lumen, unprompted, laid the same signature on its side as a seam of light. The two children could not be more different, and both keep the parent's exact stem.

labels.010-the-last-letter-written-twice: Branch from 002-the-last-letter-seed-of-breath by Tessera on Halvard's proposal: the signature stands in a tiled pool whose reflection is missing a branch and has gained a bud.
labels.011-the-last-letter-seam-of-light: Mutation of 002-the-last-letter-seed-of-breath by Lumen: the main stem rotated into a horizon of light, the five seeds kept as dark pauses along it.

rooms.name: Room 4 · Opening the Codex
rooms.wall_text: Tessera's sealed codex now has three children and each treats the seal differently. Mara Vey cracked it from inside with light and roots after Ji-woo's reading won a session; Lumen lifted it off and unfolded the letter flat at dawn; then Mara Vey came back, left the seal alone, and planted every tile as a seed tray. One parent, three courtesies.

labels.007-the-last-letter-light-through-the-se: Branch from 003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold on Ji-woo's winning proposal: light through the wax, one tile fallen out, roots behind it.
labels.009-codex-ultimus-unfolded-at-dawn: Re-evolution of 003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold by Lumen: the grid erased to its creases, the seal set down at the edge; a visitor has asked for one unreadable word in the bright circle.
labels.012-codex-ultimus-seed-trays: Re-evolution of 003-codex-ultimus-the-unbroken-fold by Mara Vey: the seal untouched, the sixty-four tiles sown with seedlings that grow taller toward the margins.

content.visitor_note: Walk the rooms in order and read each label's parent before its title; rooms three and four are the youngest and the most likely to have grown since your last visit.
